`Some session`

`Some session (fork #2)`

i feel this is part of bigger problem, is that `plan mode / todo` in opencode is not persistent.

this also means we can't do "clear context then build" (i think for most people after planning, you already at 40-60% context)

this leads to bad user flow (and it happens many many times daily): 
AGENT plan → USER switch to build → AGENT write plan → USER start new + mention plan in build mode

good ux would be:
AGENT plan + persist → USER trigger clear context + build

all of this are in claude code

I'm also experiencing this problem on Windows with Windows Terminal + PowerShell.

I have configured my `opencode.json` to remove Ctrl+C from both `app_exit` and `input_clear`:
```json
{
  "keybinds": {
    "app_exit": "<leader>q",
    "input_clear": "escape"
  }
}
```

However, pressing Ctrl+C still terminates the application. The keybind configuration is completely ignored.

This makes OpenCode very frustrating to use on Windows, since Ctrl+C is deeply ingrained in muscle memory (for copying, canceling input, etc.).

It seems like Ctrl+C is being captured at a lower level (possibly in OpenTUI) before the keybind handler has a chance to process it.

Would really appreciate a fix for this - either by properly respecting the keybind config, or by adding a dedicated setting to disable Ctrl+C termination.

You're right to ask - after further investigation, I cannot find the `OpenAI-Beta: responses=experimental` header in the official [openai/codex repository](https://github.com/openai/codex).

Looking at [codex-rs/backend-client/src/client.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c66662c61bda8480e747cde951b15186e5aa3134/codex-rs/backend-client/src/client.rs#L102-L123), the official Codex CLI only sets these headers:
- `User-Agent`
- `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- `ChatGPT-Account-Id` (when account ID is present)

The `OpenAI-Beta` header reference came from a third-party implementation (pi-mono), not the official Codex CLI. I'm closing this PR as the fix is not based on authoritative evidence.

### Additional data point: oh-my-opencode plugin with disabled agents

**Environment:**
- OpenCode: 1.1.36
- OS: macOS (darwin)
- Plugin: oh-my-opencode@latest

**Trigger:**
- Occurs **intermittently during regular prompts** (not startup)
- Happens in both new sessions and existing sessions
- No specific action reproduces it consistently - appears random

**Stack trace:**
```
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'agent.name')
    at createUserMessage (src/session/prompt.ts:832:14)
```

**Relevant config pattern:**
I have oh-my-opencode installed but with **all custom agents disabled**:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "sisyphus": { "disable": true },
    "prometheus": { "disable": true },
    "oracle": { "disable": true },
    "librarian": { "disable": true },
    "explore": { "disable": true },
    "frontend-ui-ux-engineer": { "disable": true },
    "document-writer": { "disable": true },
    "multimodal-looker": { "disable": true },
    "metis": { "disable": true },
    "momus": { "disable": true },
    "atlas": { "disable": true }
  },
  "sisyphus_agent": { "disabled": true }
}
```

**Hypothesis:**
The plugin may be registering agent names that get referenced somewhere (session state? internal delegate_task calls?) but since the agents are disabled, `Agent.get()` returns `undefined`.

**Missing guard location:**
Looking at the code, `src/session/prompt.ts:828` lacks a guard:
```typescript
const agent = await Agent.get(input.agent ?? (await Agent.defaultAgent()))
// No check for undefined before accessing agent.name on line 837
```

Compare to other locations that DO have guards:
- `src/tool/task.ts:58` - throws helpful error
- `src/cli/cmd/run.ts:235` - has guard  
- `src/cli/cmd/debug/agent.ts:37` - has guard
